q: The chemists' counting unit is named the _____, and it is defined as equal to the number of atoms in exactly 12 g of $^{12}C$.
e: The chemists' counting unit is named the mole, and it is defined as equal to the number of atoms in exactly 12 g of 12C. The mole is the chemist's counting unit, tied to 6.02 x 10^23 particles. Litre would fill a different blank than mole.

q: The number of particles in a mole is called Avogadro's constant, which is equal to _____.
e: The number of particles in a mole is called Avogadro's constant, which is equal to 6.02 x 1023. 6.02 x 1023 is the idea that completes this fact. 12.04 x 1023 would fill a different blank than 6.02 x 1023.

q: The mass of a mole of substance is referred to as its _____, and its unit is $g \ mol^{-1}$.
e: The mass of a mole of substance is referred to as its molar mass, and its unit is g mol-1. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole. Atomic mass would fill a different blank than molar mass.

q: One mole of any gas has a volume of $24 \ dm^3$ or _____ at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.).
e: One mole of any gas has a volume of 24 dm3 or 24,000 cm3 at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.). 24,000 cm3 is the idea that completes this fact. 22,400 cm3 would fill a different blank than 24,000 cm3.

q: Room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.) are often taken as conditions of _____ and 1 atmosphere.
e: Room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.) are often taken as conditions of 25 degrees C and 1 atmosphere. 25 degrees C is the idea that completes this fact. 100 degrees C would fill a different blank than 25 degrees C.

q: One mole of every gas occupies _____ at STP (standard temperature and pressure).
e: One mole of every gas occupies 22.4 dm3 at STP (standard temperature and pressure). 22.4 dm3 is the idea that completes this fact. 24,000 cm3 would fill a different blank than 22.4 dm3.

q: Standard temperature and pressure (STP) conditions are _____ and standard pressure of 760 mmHg or 1 atmosphere.
e: Standard temperature and pressure (STP) conditions are 0 degrees C or 273 K and standard pressure of 760 mmHg or 1 atmosphere. 0 degrees C or 273 K is the idea that completes this fact. 100 degrees C or 373 K would fill a different blank than 0 degrees C or 273 K.

q: To find the number of moles of a substance, you can divide the mass of the substance in grams by its _____.
e: To find the number of moles of a substance, you can divide the mass of the substance in grams by its molar mass. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole. Volume would fill a different blank than molar mass.

q: Amedeo Avogadro first deduced that equal volumes of gases contain equal number of _____ under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.
e: Amedeo Avogadro first deduced that equal volumes of gases contain equal number of molecules under the same conditions of temperature and pressure. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact. Ions would fill a different blank than molecules.

q: The Avogadro's constant applies to atoms, molecules, ions, and _____.
e: The Avogadro's constant applies to atoms, molecules, ions, and electrons. An electron is a tiny negative particle that occupies shells around the nucleus. Protons would fill a different blank than electrons.

q: A mole of chlorine molecules, $Cl_2$, contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ chlorine molecules but _____ as many chlorine atoms.
e: A mole of chlorine molecules, Cl2, contains 6.02 x 1023 chlorine molecules but twice as many chlorine atoms. Twice is the idea that completes this fact. Half would fill a different blank than twice.

q: The Systeme International (SI) unit for mass is the _____, but chemists prefer to use grams for general laboratory work.
e: The Systeme International (SI) unit for mass is the kilogram, but chemists prefer to use grams for general laboratory work. Kilogram is the idea that completes this fact. Pound would fill a different blank than kilogram.

q: To convert volumes of gases into moles at r.t.p., the volume of the gas in $dm^3$ is divided by _____.
e: To convert volumes of gases into moles at r.t.p., the volume of the gas in dm3 is divided by 24 dm3 mol-1. 24 dm3 mol-1 is the idea that completes this fact. 12 dm3 mol-1 would fill a different blank than 24 dm3 mol-1.

q: Sodium hydrogen carbonate ($NaHCO_3$), also known as baking soda, is used in the manufacture of some toothpaste and as a _____ in food production.
e: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3), also known as baking soda, is used in the manufacture of some toothpaste and as a raising agent in food production. Raising agent is the idea that completes this fact. Preservative would fill a different blank than raising agent.

q: An important element for the growth of plants, which farmers may add as artificial fertiliser if the soil is low in it, is _____.
e: An important element for the growth of plants, which farmers may add as artificial fertiliser if the soil is low in it, is nitrogen. Nitrogen is the idea that completes this fact. Phosphorus would fill a different blank than nitrogen.

q: The purity of sodium hydrogen carbonate can be obtained by measuring how much _____ is given off.
e: The purity of sodium hydrogen carbonate can be obtained by measuring how much carbon dioxide is given off. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than carbon dioxide.
